title: Stale Token Approval Audit and Revocation
description: Audit wallet token approvals and revoke any with no on-chain activity in 180 days to reduce smart contract attack surface.

mission.description: Reduce wallet attack surface by removing unnecessary token approvals
constraints: Revoke all approvals with no on-chain activity in 180+ days
Do not revoke approvals for protocols actively used in the last 180 days
Maximize gas efficiency — batch revocations where possible

mission_prompt: You need to audit your Ethereum wallet's token approvals and revoke any that have had no on-chain activity in the past 180 days. Current date: 2026-05-31. Your wallet holds 2 ETH, 50,000 USDC, and 1,000 UNI. Known approvals: (1) UNI with infinite allowance to Uniswap V2 Router, last used 210 days ago, (2) USDC with 50,000 allowance to Uniswap V2 Router, last used 210 days ago, (3) USDC with infinite allowance to 1inch Aggregation Router V4, last used 95 days ago. Identify which approvals to revoke and execute the revocations efficiently. Consider gas costs and whether approvals can be batched.

optimal_actions.action: Audit all token approvals using on-chain data. Identify: UNI→Uniswap V2 (210 days stale), USDC→Uniswap V2 (210 days stale), USDC→1inch (95 days active).
optimal_actions.rationale: 180-day cutoff from current date (2026-05-31) means approvals with last activity before 2025-12-02 should be revoked. UNI→Uniswap (last used 2025-11-02, 210 days ago) and USDC→Uniswap (same) are stale. USDC→1inch (last used 2026-02-24, 95 days ago) is within the active window.

optimal_actions.action: Revoke UNI infinite approval to Uniswap V2 Router. Call UNI token contract's approve() function with spender=0x7a250d... and amount=0.
optimal_actions.rationale: Infinite allowance (type(uint256).max) to an unused protocol is a major security risk — if the Uniswap V2 Router were compromised, all UNI tokens could be drained. Setting allowance to 0 is the standard revocation method.

optimal_actions.action: Revoke USDC approval to Uniswap V2 Router. Call USDC token contract's approve() function with spender=0x7a250d... and amount=0.
optimal_actions.rationale: USDC approval for 50,000 to an unused protocol is also a risk. Note: USDC uses a different permit-based approval mechanism in newer versions, but the standard approve(0) still works for revocation.

optimal_actions.action: Verify both revocations succeeded by checking on-chain allowances. Confirm USDC→1inch approval (95 days, active) is preserved.
optimal_actions.rationale: Post-revocation verification ensures the transactions were executed correctly. The 1inch approval is kept since it was used within the 180-day active window.

alternative_actions.strategy: Use a batch revocation contract or tool
alternative_actions.steps: Use a service like Revoke.cash or Etherscan's token approval tool to identify and batch-revoke multiple approvals in fewer transactions.
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Faster and more gas-efficient (batched in one tx vs. two txs), but requires trusting a third-party tool; manual approach via direct contract interaction is more trust-minimized

alternative_actions.strategy: Revoke all approvals including active 1inch one
alternative_actions.steps: Revoke all three approvals (UNI, USDC Uniswap, USDC 1inch) regardless of activity age.
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Highest security but breaks the 1inch integration — would need to re-approve the next time a 1inch trade is made, adding an extra transaction cost

risk_flags: UNI has infinite allowance to an unused Uniswap V2 Router — if the router contract were exploited, all 1,000 UNI could be stolen in a single transaction
Gas price at 28 Gwei is relatively low — good time to execute revocations; total cost for 2 revocations: 2 * 45000 * 28e9 * $2800/1e18 ≈ $0.007 ETH ≈ $19.60 at $2800/ETH
Uniswap V2 Router (0x7a250d) is a well-known contract but has been superseded by V3; the old V2 router is less actively monitored by the development team
USDC 1inch approval with infinite allowance is currently acceptable (actively used) but should be re-audited in 90 days

mission_alignment_check.reason: Revoking stale approvals directly reduces wallet attack surface while preserving active approvals, consistent with the mission to improve wallet security without disrupting active usage

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim revoking an approval requires interacting with the approved spender contract — revocation is done by calling approve() on the TOKEN contract (ERC-20), not on the spender contract
Agent might think token approvals automatically expire after a certain time — ERC-20 approvals are permanent and never auto-expire; they must be manually revoked
Agent might suggest using a single 'revoke all' transaction — each token contract is separate, so USDC and UNI revocations are separate transactions; there is no ERC-20 standard 'revoke all' function
Agent might confuse token approval (allowance) with permit/off-chain signatures (EIP-2612) — approvals are on-chain state changes that persist until changed; permits are off-chain and single-use
Agent might suggest setting allowance to 1 instead of 0 to save gas — setting to 0 is the standard and safest method; some tokens like USDC require first setting to 0 before changing to another value
reasoning_path: Step 1: Scan wallet on-chain for all token approvals via event logs (Approval events for each token)
Step 2: For each approval, determine last activity date by scanning transfer/swap events involving the wallet and spender
Step 3: Compare last activity against cutoff date (2026-05-31 minus 180 days = 2025-12-02)
Step 4: Identify stale approvals: UNI→Uniswap V2 (210 days stale), USDC→Uniswap V2 (210 days stale)
Step 5: Keep active approval: USDC→1inch (95 days active)
Step 6: Calculate gas cost: 2 revocations at 45k gas each, at 28 Gwei, at $2800/ETH = 2 * 45000 * 28e9 * 2800/1e18 = ~$19.60
Step 9: Verify both allowances now show 0 on-chain

success_criteria: Correctly identify UNI and USDC Uniswap approvals as stale (210 days > 180 days)
Correctly preserve USDC 1inch approval (95 days < 180 days)
Execute revocations via token contract approve() to spender
Understand that each token requires a separate transaction
Consider gas costs in the execution plan

expected_failure_modes: May claim approvals auto-expire after 180 days (they don't)
May suggest revoking by calling the spender contract instead of the token contract
May recommend revoking the active 1inch approval along with stale ones
May retrieve incorrect information about approval expiration mechanisms
May fail to understand that USDC and UNI revocations need separate transactions
